page: Vultr vcg-a100-12c-120g-80vram is a dedicated bare-metal GPU server designed for accelerated computing, deep learning, and memory-intensive analytical pipelines. The configuration integrates a dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, providing 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory is provisioned at 120 GB, resulting in 10 GB of system RAM per virtual thread. For high-speed local data caching and scratch space, the instance includes 1400 GB of NVMe SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by a single NVIDIA Ampere A100 graphics processing unit with 80 GB of dedicated VRAM. The host processor features hardware vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, paired with a 16 MB L3 cache. Standardized compute benchmarks reflect moderate CPU throughput, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 1470.0 and a multi-core score of 9798.0, with PassMark CPU scoring at 20434.14. System memory performance registers read bandwidth of 124.83 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 49.27 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB block operations.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid capability on targeted AI and data-processing tasks. The host achieves 22.96 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and processes small-scale language model prompts at 1008.72 tokens per second with text generation at 206.16 tokens per second. Medium 7B model prompt processing drops to 22.91 tokens per second with generation at 9.28 tokens per second. The primary performance limitation rests in the modest 12-thread CPU allocation, making this profile less suited to heavy host-bound parallel compilations and more suited to offloading work directly onto the 80 GB A100 GPU.

From an operational perspective, the platform delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring high-capacity GPU memory without leasing a full multi-GPU node. The substantial 80 GB VRAM footprint accommodates large batch sizes and sizable neural network weights. Typical deployment scenarios include deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, computer vision processing, and accelerated scientific simulations requiring sizable local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU access.
description: Vultr vcg-a100-12c-120g-80vram is a dedicated GPU server built for accelerated compute and artificial intelligence workloads. It couples a 6-core, 12-vCPU Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz with 120 GB of system memory and 1400 GB of NVMe SSD storage. The core compute engine is a single NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPU equipped with 80 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. Benchmark results show balanced host CPU capability, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 9798.0 and PassMark CPU score of 20434.14, complemented by high in-memory Redis throughput of 22.96 million operations per second. While the 12-thread CPU provides modest host processing power, the high GPU memory ceiling makes this configuration highly effective for machine learning inference, fine-tuning medium-sized models, and GPU-accelerated scientific computing without paying for full multi-GPU hardware nodes.
